title: Automate provisioning and rotation of external audit sinks (S3/GCS) for Private installs
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Context: Private customers require an automated, auditable way to export cluster audit logs to long-term external archives (S3/GCS) with enforced retention and rotated credentials. This PR adds end-to-end automation across the private installer, Helm chart wiring, and Terraform module to provision external buckets, create rotation schedules for exporter credentials, and apply retention lifecycle rules. Motivation: reduce manual steps during onboarding and to ensure retention policies are consistently applied for compliance audits. Scope: 1) Terraform module `audit_sink` that creates bucket, IAM/service account bindings, lifecycle retention rules, and optional KMS key bindings; 2) Helm chart templates and values to accept external sink configuration and secrets references; 3) Installer hooks (private-installer) to call Terraform and render Helm values during install/upgrade; 4) A small credentials-rotation utility (rotate_sinks.sh) and systemd timer that runs in the private control-plane for automatic key rotation; 5) Migration docs + upgrade/rollback considerations. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module implemented and unit-tested with terratest mocks - [x] Helm changes wired and backward-compatible for clusters that don't use external sinks - [x] Installer integration for both initial provision and upgrades - [x] Rotation utility + basic E2E in an internal staging cluster - [x] RBAC checks and audit events emitted for provisioning actions - [x] Docs and an upgrade playbook created Breaking behaviour: none expected for clusters without `externalAuditSink` set. For clusters enabling sinks, a permissions grant is required; installer will pause and surface a clear checklist if permissions are missing. Migration notes: existing manual buckets are left untouched unless `migrateExisting: true` is provided; migration performs an incremental copy and updates exporter config to point to the provisioned bucket. Rollback considerations: Helm values are applied in a staged manner, and the installer records Terraform state snapshots under /var/lib/redwood/audit-sink/tfstate-backups to simplify rollback. Commits summary: - feat(terraform): add audit_sink module with bucket, lifecycle, kms and outputs - feat(helm): add templates/external-sink-secret.yaml and values.externalAuditSink - feat(installer): hook to call terraform apply and render helm values - feat(rotate): add rotate_sinks.sh + systemd unit + basic smoke check - docs: upgrade playbook and operator checklist - test: terratest for bucket creation and lifecycle rules CI: initial run showed a lint failure in helm templates (missing required annotations) which was fixed in a follow-up commit; integration tests run against an isolated staging project (GCP/S3 matrix) and passed on the final run. Files changed (high level): - terraform/modules/audit_sink/main.tf (new) - terraform/modules/audit_sink/outputs.tf (new) - terraform/modules/audit_sink/variables.tf (new) - helm/audit-log-exporter/templates/external-sink-secret.yaml (new) - helm/audit-log-exporter/values.schema.json (updated) - installer/hooks/provision-audit-sink.sh (new) - installer/assets/tfstate-backup.service (new) - tools/rotate_sinks.sh (new) - docs/private/audit-sink-upgrade.md (new) - ci/terratest/audit_sink_test.go (new) Small snippet: helm template adds annotations for audit-log-exporter to pick up external sink config: annotations: "redwood.audit/external-sink: {{ .Values.externalAuditSink.enabled }}" Review discussion: - Aisha: "Please add a terratest case that asserts lifecycle rule 'Delete' after X days and KMS binding when kms_key_id is provided." Reply (Priya): "Added a terratest matrix for GCS/S3 and an explicit assert for lifecycle rules (see ci/terratest/audit_sink_test.go)." - Marco: "Installer should not auto-apply terraform if --dry-run is set; ensure idempotency on re-runs." Reply (Priya): "Installer respects DRY_RUN env and will save a plan file; added tests for repeated runs producing same plan." - Ellen: "Rotation interval 30 days is aggressive for some customers; can we make it configurable per-cluster?" Reply (Priya): "Made rotate interval a cluster-level Helm value with default 90d and documented tradeoffs in the playbook." Approval flow: - Marco approved after idempotency tests were added - Aisha approved after terratest additions - Ellen gave final sign-off for release notes and config knobs CI details: - lint (helm/python/terraform) -> initially failed (helm annotation), rerun -> pass - unit tests -> pass - integration (staging projects) -> pass - security-scan (tfsec + trivy) -> pass Merge notes: squashed merge to main; migration playbook included as part of the merge commit message. Backout plan: revert the merge and apply tfstate snapshot from /var/lib/redwood/audit-sink/tfstate-backups if an emergency rollback is needed.
